Chapter 264: Xiaonei Users Surpass Ten Million

By the time Chen Guiliang finished recording *Dialogue* at CCTV, it was already September 6th.

There's not much to say about the recording; he basically repeated what he had said to the aunties a few days ago, this time for the *Dialogue* program.

Chen Guiliang was the main guest, with two professors as the other guests.

One professor believed that minors should be banned from playing games, while the other believed that children should be guided to play healthy games.

The studio audience came from all walks of life, and most were against online games.

Then Chen Guiliang found himself under siege.

Some parents even said that all internet cafes in the country should be shut down.

If CCTV's *Dialogue* didn't change its format, Chen Guiliang wouldn't be coming back next time. The recording was mentally exhausting.

"Boss, the Internet Society of China has sent an invitation for you to attend this year's China Internet Conference on the 21st of this month." Secretary Hu Yuexia came in with a letter.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Is there anything special this year?"

Hu Yuexia replied, "It's on a particularly large scale, and the higher-ups are taking it very seriously. The head of the Ministry of Information Industry, the bosses of China Mobile and China Unicom, and the CEOs of the major internet giants are all going to be there."

"Got it. You handle the arrangements," Chen Guiliang said.

Chen Guiliang buried his head in other reports, and Hu Yuexia closed the door as she left.

Xiami Music had officially launched and begun to interact with Xiaonei and Hainei. As this year's freshmen successively arrived at their universities, the three platforms would jointly launch an "Original Music Online Contest" in mid-September.

As university enrollment continued to expand, the number of undergraduate and junior college students in the second half of the year had already soared to 17.388 million.

Over the past few days, a large number of freshmen had registered on Xiaonei.

According to the website's backend data, the number of currently enrolled undergraduate and junior college student users on Xiaonei had surpassed the 7 million mark yesterday.

That was equivalent to 40% of all enrolled undergraduate and junior college students having registered an account on Xiaonei. This proportion was even higher than the rate of computer ownership among university students!

Regardless of whether they used it frequently, they would be pulled in by classmates to at least register an account.

In addition, Xiaonei had over 500,000 enrolled graduate student users (Master's and PhD), over 30,000 adult education student users, and over 2 million high school, vocational high school, and secondary technical school student users. There were also over 1.4 million graduated users who still occasionally interacted on Xiaonei.

The total user count had reached 10.56 million!

Over the next one or two months, a large number of new students would continue to register.

This figure was not inflated, nor did it involve repeat registrations, because it was all based on a real-name system. At worst, users might register and not use their accounts, which would then become zombie accounts.

This morning, Xiaonei had already announced the data, with the good news posted on the homepage in bold, red font.

When Zhang Fan, the CEO of Zhanzuo.com, heard the news, he sat in his office, speechless for a long time.

He had successively converted nearly 1 million student users through Eyou Mailbox.

He had also spent a crazy amount of money on offline promotions and had even collaborated officially with the Communist Youth League, the China Youth Daily, and major universities. The "Inspirational University Student" selection event hosted by Zhanzuo.com was actually organized by the Youth League, and the awards were presented in person by a Youth League leader.

Nearly all members of the student unions at major renowned universities had registered accounts on Zhanzuo.com.

But the user count hadn't grown for a long time, currently sitting at just over 1.6 million.

Moreover, many of these 1.6 million users had already become zombie accounts, having long since moved over to Xiaonei.

Campus social networking is a relatively closed loop, heavily influenced by offline factors.

This was different from the broad social networking of Hainei, which could accommodate many different websites.

A closed social network can only have one dominant player; the minority will follow the majority. Otherwise, they risk being seen as unsociable, and an active social ecosystem cannot form.

One step ahead, every step ahead!

The fast eat the meat, the slow eat shit.

Zhang Fan felt as awful as if he were eating shit right now. He had no way to answer to his investors and could only discuss how to shut down Zhanzuo.com.

In this era of venture capital madness, anyone could get investment.

What's more, Zhanzuo.com had over a million users, as well as the backing of the Youth League, the China Youth Daily, and major universities.

Relying on these, Zhang Fan had managed to attract several million US dollars in venture capital funding. Among them, Sequoia Capital alone had invested 2 million US dollars.

The most infuriating thing was that in Zhanzuo.com's first "Inspirational University Student" selection, user votes had placed Chen Guiliang sixth (out of 10 total)... Fortunately, Chen Guiliang didn't attend the award ceremony, otherwise, it would have been incredibly awkward.

Zhang Fan picked up his phone and called an investor. "Hello, Mr. Shen, this is Zhang Fan from Zhanzuo.com... Yes, that's right... I'm calling about something. I plan to shut down Zhanzuo.com."

"What did you say?" The voice on the other end was utterly shocked.

Zhang Fan sighed, "Xiaonei's user count has surpassed 10 million. As for our Zhanzuo.com, it hasn't grown much in recent months, and user activity is getting lower and lower. I'm not planning on doing offline promotions for the new freshmen this year. Every bit saved is something."

The investor was too angry to speak. After a long silence, he finally asked, "Is it really hopeless?"

Zhang Fan said, "It really is. Besides Xiaonei, no other campus social networking site in the country can survive. I will stop all non-essential expenses on my end. You and the other investors should send someone over to audit our financial situation as soon as possible."

"Sigh... alright then," the investor sighed.

Venture capital. The word "risk" comes first.

If Zhanzuo.com shut down, Xiaonei would have a near-monopoly in the campus social networking sector.

Of course, there was still QQ Qzone, which was indirectly snatching up market share, having taken away too many middle school student users.

The news of Xiaonei's user count surpassing 10 million quickly spread to other internet companies, and even some industry giants were shocked.

Because behind those accounts were a solid 10 million real people!

"Hello, this is Xiaonei... If Lenovo wants to place another ad next week, the advertising fee will be increasing slightly... It's not a price hike out of nowhere, Xiaonei's users have surpassed ten million. Not the ten million from other websites with repeat registrations, ours are all real-name registrations. The ad fee for a website with ten million users is bound to increase a bit, because the effect will be better..."

Xiaonei's salespeople were now much more confident when making calls.

Due to many students complaining that the side banners were uncomfortable to look at, Xiaonei had already removed them.

Now, only banner ads remained.

The banner ads were divided into the website homepage banner, category homepage banners, and personal homepage banners.

It seemed like a lot, but the pages were actually very clean. Besides the one at the very top of the webpage, the rest was completely clear.

This time, with the price increase, the website homepage banner ad shot up to 50,000 yuan a day!

Moreover, special dates would be priced differently.

For example, during the back-to-school season for freshmen, many new students would buy electronics. Placing an ad at this time would surely have a particularly good effect, so the advertising fee would naturally be higher.

Brands like Lenovo, Hasee, Nokia, and Motorola were major clients during the back-to-school season.

"Mr. Chen, congratulations," Yang Lin, Vice President of Carlyle Asia, called to offer her congratulations.

Chen Guiliang laughed, "Congratulations to you too. Let's all make money together."

Yang Lin asked, "Xiaonei's market share among university students should be over 50% by now, right?"

Chen Guiliang gave a vague answer, "Just about."

Yang Lin remarked with emotion, "That is a very astonishing achievement. And Hainei's user count also broke 10 million before. Two websites with user levels in the tens of millions, plus investments in the fast-growing Kuaishou gaming company and video website. That's more than qualified for a NASDAQ listing."

"Let's wait. Next year's performance will definitely be better," Chen Guiliang said.

Yang Lin knew Chen Guiliang was stubborn, so she said in a consultative tone, "How about we start planning for an IPO early next year? I'll contact the other investors for you. You'll also need to hire an executive specifically responsible for the IPO. We can recommend one, but whether you use them or not is up to you."

"Okay, you can jointly recommend someone. But I'll need to talk to this person first," Chen Guiliang said.

Yang Lin's mood improved even more. Acting like a caring big sister, she chatted with Chen Guiliang for another ten minutes or so.

Not long after hanging up, investors from firms like IDG and DFJ also called one after another to offer congratulations and brought up the matter of an IPO as well.

IDG, in particular, was a firm that favored small-scale investments with quick entries and exits, and they had long been hoping ByteDance would go public soon.

Carlyle, on the other hand, leaned towards long-term operations, often holding onto shares for several years after a company went public. But they liked to help optimize companies, often giving pointers to the businesses they invested in.

"Senior, I'm at the school!" Tao Xue called, her voice full of delight.

Chen Guiliang said, "Didn't I tell you to call ahead so I could pick you up from the airport?"

"No need to trouble you, haha. We have military training in a few days. I've never done it before, you know. When I started high school, it was during the SARS outbreak, and military training was canceled," Tao Xue said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Buy plenty of sanitary pads to use as shoe insoles."
